correctness.rationale: The covolume of the honeycomb translation lattice is 3*sqrt(3)/2 with two sites per cell. Thus at d=2/sqrt(39) the scaled density is 13/sqrt(3), so 2*sqrt(3)*rho=26. A center in the chosen fundamental parallelogram has norm at most sqrt(3) in Euclidean length; any enclosed honeycomb site has squared norm strictly below 24. Independently enumerated candidates using (X,Y)=(2a-b,b) with the metric X^2+3Y^2 and exact squared radical comparisons. A leftmost feasible center of the intersection of the disks about any contained set either has two active boundaries or is a left tip of a single active circle. Translate that candidate into the tile, translating its sites with it. The computation checks 192 pair descriptions and two single-active tips, maximum 26, precisely the six stated half-coordinate classes and exactly two diameter pairs in opposite norm-39 unit orbits at each one. Any original 26-site set must coincide, after translation, with the complete 26-site set of its extremal candidate; a diameter pair fixes the sole possible original center. No 27-site disk survives even at a candidate. Published Lemma 3.14 applies to any hypothetical covering (no periodicity assumption), using closedness in its limiting argument. Its triangular-lattice replacement has all centers in the half-integral class union. For a shortest vector v in unscaled coordinates, N(2v)=156 forces even Eisenstein coordinates of 2v by parity; thus N(v)=39 implies v lies in Lambda. The center period lattice v Z[omega] has index 13 in Lambda, so it yields 26 honeycomb residue classes. A disk's norm-39 diameter pair in the unit orbit of v repeats a residue and the disk misses a class. The translated disks cannot cover that class.
